title: LegoZK: A Dynamically Reconfigurable Accelerator for Zero-Knowledge Proof
problem: Existing ZKP accelerators are designed at the granularity of core operators and exhibit low hardware resource utilization and limited adaptability across the different computation stages of proof generation (e.g., NTT, MSM, polynomial operations).
motivation: Zero-knowledge proofs enable privacy-preserving applications, but the huge overhead of proof generation (dominated by finite field arithmetic) impedes widespread adoption, and current accelerators cannot efficiently reconfigure to serve all ZKP computation stages.
method: LegoZK uses finite field arithmetic units (FAUs) as fundamental building blocks integrated via a hierarchical on-chip NoC. By dynamically configuring the FAUs and the NoC interconnect at runtime, LegoZK can target each computation stage of proof generation without hardware specialization per stage. For the most time-consuming stage (Multi-Scalar Multiplication, MSM), LegoZK proposes a fast, fully pipelined bucket reduction algorithm based on lookup tables, significantly reducing MSM latency. The NoC topology and FAU configuration are switched between proof stages.
key_novelty: Using finite field arithmetic units as universal reconfigurable primitives connected by a hierarchical NoC allows a single hardware design to efficiently accelerate all stages of ZKP proof generation, rather than requiring per-operator specialization.
contributions: Dynamically reconfigurable ASIC using FAUs as fundamental components connected via hierarchical NoC for all ZKP computation stages
Fast fully pipelined lookup-table-based bucket reduction algorithm for MSM
31.96x speedup over ZKP ASIC PipeZK and 11.30x over GPU accelerator GZKP
50.1% area reduction and 37.7% power reduction vs. PipeZK

metrics.speedup: 31.96x over PipeZK (ASIC); 11.30x over GZKP (GPU) in proof generation

primary_theme: dynamically reconfigurable ASIC for zero-knowledge proof generation
